backlog.title: URL Shape Gate and Notify Bugfix Release
backlog.description: Fix the two bugs identified in the end-to-end validation PRD: BUG-001 (Major) — the URL_SHAPE_RE gate matches common code-file extensions as alpha-TLD hostnames, causing unwanted network fetches and content injection for everyday coding prose like '#main.go'. BUG-002 (Minor) — the status toast says '#@ injected' even for URL-only injections. Both fixes are localized to file-injector.ts and its test suite, with no API surface changes.

milestones.title: BUG-001: Eliminate code-extension false-positives in URL detection
milestones.description: Tighten the URL shape gate so scheme-less tokens whose final label is a known code/file extension (go, md, py, rs, ts, json, png, csv, etc.) are NOT treated as URLs. This prevents unwanted network egress and content injection for everyday '#filename.ext' coding prompts while preserving legitimate bare-domain URL detection (example.com, api.example.co.uk) and explicit-scheme URLs (#https://anything).

tasks.title: Implement code-extension deny-list gate in the URL scan loop
tasks.description: Add a comprehensive CODE_EXTENSIONS Set constant and a post-gate check in the URL scan loop that rejects scheme-less tokens whose final label matches a known code/file extension. Update the URL_SHAPE_RE JSDoc to document the new behavior.

subtasks.title: Add CODE_EXTENSIONS deny-list constant and integrate the gate in the URL scan loop

tasks.title: Regression tests for the tightened URL shape gate
tasks.description: Update the COL-4 test case (#node.js now blocked by the deny-list) and add comprehensive no-fetch regression tests for representative #filename.ext patterns. Add a test proving that even a 200-OK response for a false-positive domain no longer injects content.

subtasks.title: Update COL-4 and add no-fetch regression tests for #filename.ext patterns
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/010_8645157f3bf5/bugfix/001_07ad0d602ba9/architecture/test_analysis.md (§5, §6, §11) and source_analysis.md (§2, §8, §11). The test file url-injection.test.mjs uses the runCase(n, name, fn) pattern with a global `calls` array and per-test globalThis.fetch stubbing via try/finally restore. COL-4 (L400-410) currently asserts #node.js IS url-shaped, fetch IS called (calls.length===1), 404 → verbatim. The test harness loads the real extension via jiti: `const mod = await jiti.import(TS_PATH)`. The FIX = FIX object is `{ cwd: TMPDIR }`. The RICH_HTML fixture (L~200) is a multi-paragraph HTML doc that passes the 200-char SPA floor. makeRes({ct, body, status, ok, contentLength}) is the response factory. Every test uses `mod.injectFiles(prompt, [], FIX, false, enableUrls)`.
2. INPUT: The tightened URL scan loop from P1.M1.T1.S1 — scheme-less tokens whose final label is in CODE_EXTENSIONS no longer pass the gate. #node.js (ext 'js') is now blocked. #main.go (ext 'go') is now blocked. #example.com (TLD 'com') is NOT blocked (com is not a code extension). Explicit-scheme tokens like #https://node.js bypass the deny-list.
3. LOGIC: (a) UPDATE COL-4 (L400-410): change the assertions from 'fetch IS called' to 'fetch is NOT called'. The new COL-4 should assert calls.length===0, injected===0, and r.text==='#node.js' (verbatim). Update the test name/comment to reflect that #node.js is now correctly rejected by the CODE_EXTENSIONS deny-list (not because it fails URL_SHAPE_RE, but because 'js' is a code extension). (b) ADD a new test group 'BUG-001 REGRESSION: code-extension tokens must NOT fetch' with individual runCase entries for representative extensions from the PRD: #main.go, #notes.md, #config.json, #image.png, #script.py, #utils.rs, #spec.tsx, #app.cs, #lib.java, #data.csv. Each case: stub fetch to record calls, call injectFiles with enableUrls=true, assert calls.length===0, injected===0, and r.text === prompt (verbatim). Use the existing calls-spy + try/finally restore pattern. (c) ADD a content-injection-harm test: stub fetch to return makeRes({ct:'text/html', body:RICH_HTML, status:200, ok:true}) and call injectFiles('refactor #main.go now', [], FIX, false, true). Assert injected===0 and that NO block contains 'https://main.go' — proving the Go homepage is NOT delivered to the model even when the domain would resolve and return rich HTML. (d) ADD a bypass test: verify explicit-scheme tokens STILL work — injectFiles('#https://node.js', [], FIX, false, true) with a fetch stub should still call fetch (calls.length===1) because explicit scheme bypasses the deny-list. This proves the deny-list only affects scheme-less tokens. Mock fetch to return makeRes({status:404, ok:false}) for the bypass test so it's hermetic. Place all new cases after the existing COLLISION group, before the NORMALIZATION group, following the existing naming convention (e.g., BUG1-1 through BUG1-N).
4. OUTPUT: Modified url-injection.test.mjs with: updated COL-4, new regression test group (~12-14 new cases), and a bypass test. All new tests must pass with the tightened gate from P1.M1.T1.S1. The full suite (npm test) must still exit 0.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change from test additions.

milestones.title: BUG-002: Trigger-aware status notify for URL-only injections
milestones.description: Make the input handler's notify toast trigger-aware so that URL-only prompts do not report '#@ injected'. Use the existing details[].kind field to distinguish URL vs file injections and produce appropriate wording for each case (files only, URLs only, mixed).

tasks.title: Implement trigger-aware notify wording in the input handler
tasks.description: Update the input handler's notify string (L1493-1495) to compute URL and file counts from the details array and produce trigger-aware wording. No API change to injectFiles is needed — the details array already carries the kind breakdown.

subtasks.title: Update notify to distinguish URL vs file injections using details[].kind
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/010_8645157f3bf5/bugfix/001_07ad0d602ba9/architecture/source_analysis.md (§5, §9) and test_analysis.md (§7, §8). The notify is at file-injector.ts:1493-1495: `const whole = injected - paged; const msg = \`#@ injected ${whole} whole${paged > 0 ? \`, ${paged} paged\` : ""}\`; if (ctx.hasUI) ctx.ui.notify(msg, "info");`. The injectFiles return destructures `injected, paged, blocks, details` at L1483. The details array has entries with kind: 'url' | 'text' | 'image' | 'binary' — one per successful delivery. details.length === injected === state.count. URLs never increment paged. The handler is inside `pi.on('input', ...)` at L1478.
2. INPUT: From injectFiles return (L1483): `details: FileDetail[]` where each FileDetail has a `kind` field. `injected` (total count) and `paged` (file-only paged count) are also available. No new return fields are needed — the existing details array provides the URL/file breakdown.
3. LOGIC: (a) After the `pending = { blocks, details }` line (L1488) and before the notify block (L1493), compute: `const urlCount = details.filter(d => d.kind === 'url').length;` and `const fileCount = injected - urlCount;`. (b) Replace the hardcoded notify msg with trigger-aware logic: If urlCount === 0 (files only, the common case): keep the EXACT existing string `#@ injected ${whole} whole${paged > 0 ? \`, ${paged} paged\` : ''}` where whole = injected - paged. If fileCount === 0 (URLs only): use `injected ${urlCount} URL${urlCount > 1 ? 's' : ''}` — NO '#@' prefix, NO 'whole'/'paged' axis. If both > 0 (mixed): use `#@ injected ${fileWhole} whole${paged > 0 ? \`, ${paged} paged\` : ''}, ${urlCount} URL${urlCount > 1 ? 's' : ''}` where fileWhole = fileCount - paged. (c) The notify type stays 'info' and the `if (ctx.hasUI)` guard stays unchanged. (d) Write the failing test FIRST: add a handler-level test in url-injection.test.mjs (or file-injector.test.mjs) that drives the input handler with a URL-only prompt (stub fetch to return makeRes with RICH_HTML) and asserts the notify does NOT contain '#@'. Then implement the fix. Then verify.
4. OUTPUT: Modified file-injector.ts L1493-1495 area with trigger-aware notify logic. The injectFiles return shape is UNCHANGED (no new fields). Existing file-only notify behavior is byte-for-byte preserved (urlCount===0 path). Only the msg string construction changes.
5. DOCS: none — the notify wording is a transient UI toast, not a documented API surface. No README or JSDoc change needed for the toast text itself.

subtasks.title: Add regression tests for URL-only and mixed prompt notify wording
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/010_8645157f3bf5/bugfix/001_07ad0d602ba9/architecture/test_analysis.md (§7). The handler-level test pattern uses captureHandler('input') to get the input callback, makeMockCtx(cwd, {hasUI:true}) to get a ctx with a notify spy, then calls `await slot.cb({text, source:'interactive', images:[]}, ctx)`. The notify spy records `rec.notify = {m, t}`. For URL tests, a fetch stub MUST be provided because injectFiles calls fetch for URL tokens — use the makeRes factory with RICH_HTML body and status:200/ok:true. The test harness must capture the 'input' handler specifically (there are also session_start and before_agent_start handlers). Note: the input handler reads the module-level `cfg` which is initialized on session_start — the test must either call the session_start handler first or ensure cfg defaults ({}) produce enableUrls !== false (which they do, since undefined !== false is true). The captureHandler pattern returns {cb, all} where cb is the LAST handler for the event.
2. INPUT: The trigger-aware notify logic from P1.M2.T1.S1 — URL-only prompts produce 'injected N URL[s]', file-only prompts produce '#@ injected N whole[, M paged]', mixed prompts produce both parts.
3. LOGIC: Add test cases (in url-injection.test.mjs or file-injector.test.mjs, following the runCase convention): (a) URL-ONLY notify test: capture ALL handlers via captureAllHandlers() (to get session_start + input + before_agent_start). Call session_start first to init cfg. Stub globalThis.fetch to return makeRes({ct:'text/html', body:RICH_HTML}). Drive the input handler with {text:'see #example.com', source:'interactive', images:[]}. Assert rec.notify.m does NOT contain '#@'. Assert rec.notify.m contains 'URL'. Assert rec.notify.t === 'info'. Restore fetch in finally. (b) MIXED notify test: write a local file fixture (file.txt) in TMPDIR. Stub fetch for the URL part. Drive input with {text:'#@file.txt and #example.com', source:'interactive', images:[]}. Assert notify.m contains BOTH 'whole' (for the file) and 'URL' (for the URL). Assert '#@' IS present (because there ARE files). Restore fetch and clean up the fixture in finally. (c) FILE-ONLY regression test: ensure the EXISTING file-only behavior is unchanged — drive input with '#@file.txt' (after writing the fixture) and assert notify.m === '#@ injected 1 whole' (byte-for-byte). This guards against regressions in the common case.
4. OUTPUT: New test cases (3-4 cases) added to the test suite. All must pass with the trigger-aware notify from P1.M2.T1.S1. The full suite (npm test) must still exit 0.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change from test additions.

subtasks.title: Update README.md URL detection documentation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/010_8645157f3bf5/bugfix/001_07ad0d602ba9/architecture/source_analysis.md (§12) and fix_strategy.md. README.md L202 currently states: 'URLs need a dotted, alphabetic hostname. A #<url> token must be a http(s):// / ftp:// URL or a bare host whose final label is 2+ letters (e.g. example.com, api.example.co.uk). This deliberately rejects #3.14, #v1.2, #fff and other token-like text.' This framing gives false confidence that #filename.ext is safe. The README also has URL documentation at L50-55 (feature examples) and L184 (enableUrls config). The README is the only user-facing doc.
2. INPUT: The completed BUG-001 fix (P1.M1.T1.S1) adds a CODE_EXTENSIONS deny-list that blocks scheme-less tokens whose final label is a known code/file extension. Explicit-scheme tokens (#https://domain.ext) bypass the deny-list. The completed BUG-002 fix (P1.M2.T1.S1) makes the notify trigger-aware.
3. LOGIC: (a) Update the 'URLs need a dotted, alphabetic hostname' bullet (README.md L202) to document the code-extension deny-list. Add a sentence explaining that scheme-less tokens ending in a common code/file extension (go, md, py, rs, ts, json, png, csv, etc.) are treated as file references, not URLs, to avoid unwanted network fetches for everyday coding prompts. State the workaround: to fetch a domain whose TLD collides with a code extension, use the explicit-scheme form (e.g. #https://foo.py instead of #foo.py). Remove or qualify the '#3.14/#v1.2/#fff rejected' framing to avoid implying #filename.ext is also safe (it was never safe before this fix, and is now explicitly handled). (b) Do NOT change the feature examples (L50-55) or the enableUrls config section (L184) unless the deny-list behavior warrants a note there — it does not (the deny-list is always active when enableUrls is on, not a separate config). (c) Ensure the README is consistent with the updated JSDoc from P1.M1.T1.S1.
4. OUTPUT: Modified README.md with the updated URL detection documentation. The change is confined to the Limits section (around L202). No structural changes to the README.
5. DOCS: This IS the documentation task — it syncs the changeset-level README documentation for both BUG-001 and BUG-002. Per §5 Mode B, it is the FINAL task that sweeps the overview docs.
